results.evidence: tests/test_evidence_published_age.py::test_old_publication_read_today_is_refused sets max_age=90, deletes all evidence, inserts a single row with observed_at = today (2026-11-30) and published_at = 120 days earlier, then runs prepare-send. It asserts exactly one 'refused: evidence:' line, that the published date is in that line, and that the prepare_refused activity lists 'evidence' in its checks. Running .venv/bin/pytest on the file in the worktree gave 4 passed. I did not mutate the code to confirm the test fails without the fix.
results.quote:
assert published in line
    assert line == f"refused: evidence: newest evidence published {published} is older than 90 days"

results.evidence: test_review_age_counts_from_publication sets the only evidence to published 120 days ago and observed today, with max_age=90. It runs `cottonwood review` and asserts that lead 1's row in the direct-candidate table has a cell '120 (over 90)'. The test file ran with .venv/bin/pytest in the worktree and all 4 tests passed.

tests/test_evidence_published_age.py::test_without_publication_date_observed_date_is_used inserts evidence with published_at=NULL and observed_at=today (2026-11-30). It checks that the review row's age cell next to the URL is "0". It also checks that prepare-send gives no 'refused: evidence:' line, and the helper cross-checks that against the prepare_refused activity checks. I ran the file with the worktree's .venv/bin/pytest and all 4 tests passed.

test_newest_publication_date_wins in tests/test_evidence_published_age.py inserts two evidence rows for lead 1 (published 200 days ago and 10 days ago, both observed today). It asserts that the review row contains the 10-day-old URL, doesn't contain the 200-day-old URL, and shows age '10' in the next cell. It then asserts prepare-send gives no 'refused: evidence:' line. The helper also checks that the prepare_refused activity's checks don't include 'evidence'. I ran the file with the worktree's .venv/bin/pytest and all 4 tests passed. The AC says 200 and 10 days, and the test uses exactly those. I did not run mutation probes, so I haven't shown the test fails when the age logic is broken.

SKILL.md diff adds a rule to record published_at when the page shows a publication date, and adds published_at to the evidence item shape. Run from the worktree's own .venv/bin, all four checks exit 0: pytest 903 passed, ruff check 'All checks passed!', mypy 'no issues found in 101 source files', ruff format --check '306 files already formatted'.
results.quote: - When the page shows a publication date, record it as the evidence item's `published_at` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Evidence age is measured from it, so an old article read today counts as old.
